To express the number in Cartesian form, we expand the parentheses and substitute the values of the cosine and sine.

First, we find $\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{2\pi }{3})$ and $\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{2\pi }{3}):$

$$
\begin{aligned}\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{2\pi }{3}) & =-\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{\pi }{3}) \\  & =-\frac{1}{2}\,,\end{aligned}
$$

$$
\begin{aligned}\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{2\pi }{3}) & =\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{\pi }{3}) \\  & =\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}\,.\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we substitute the values and expand the parentheses:

$$
\begin{aligned}z & =18(\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{2\pi }{3})+\text{i}\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{2\pi }{3})) \\  & =18(-\frac{1}{2}+\text{i}\,\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}) \\  & =-\frac{18}{2}+\text{i}\,\frac{18\sqrt{3}}{2} \\  & =-9+9\sqrt{3}\,\text{i}\end{aligned}
$$
